chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his daughter to his brother's son, and gave her as dower a house and a servant. Then the man died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The dower is taken from the middle of the wealth.' I said: 'And the house and the servant?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The middle of the houses, and the servant is the middle of the servants.' I said: 'Thirty or forty dinars, and the house is about that much.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is seventy, eighty dinars, or a hundred, about that much.'

key_terms.دِينَار: Gold dinar, a unit of currency
key_terms.مَهْر: Dower or dowry given by the groom to the bride

ai.seo_question: How is the value of specific dower assets like a house and servant calculated for inheritance purposes in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the method for determining the 'middle' (wasat) of wealth when specific non-monetary assets like a house and servant are part of the dower, establishing a precedent for equitable valuation in inheritance. The Imam provides a practical benchmark, suggesting that such assets typically hold a value equivalent to 70-80 or up to 100 dinars, reflecting the economic norms of the time. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and avoiding arbitrary valuation when settling financial obligations from an estate.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about a man who got his daughter married to a son of his brother, and made a house and a servant to be her dower. Then the man died. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The dower would be taken from the average of the wealth’. I said, ‘So the house and the servant?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An average from the houses, and the servant is an average from the servants’. I said, ‘Thirty or fourty Dinars, and the house is approximately that’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is seventy, eighty Dinars, or a hundred, approximately that’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who gave his daughter in marriage to the son of his brother with a mahr (dower) of a house and a servant and the man died. He (the Imam) said, ‘Mahr (dower) is paid from medium kinds of assets.’ I (the narrator) than asked, ‘What is the condition of the house and servant?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The house must be of a medium condition and the servant must be of a medium condition.’ I then asked, ‘Can it be thirty or forty dinar? The house is about that much.’ The Imam said, ‘This is seventy-eighty dinar or one hundred dinar or so.’”
